children: Greenbriar Equity Group is close to a deal to buy aerospace and defense supplier Spectrum Control for more than $1.8 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the talks.

Greenbriar emerged ahead of competing industrial bidders for Spectrum Control, which is owned by private equity firm AEA Investors. An agreement could be announced as soon as this week, although negotiations could still fall apart or another buyer could emerge.
Greenbriar and AEA declined to comment to Bloomberg. Spectrum Control didn’t respond to a request for comment.

The potential acquisition highlights continued demand for suppliers serving the aerospace, defense and space markets. Spectrum Control makes radio-frequency, microwave and other electronic components used in communications systems designed to operate in demanding environments. A deal above $1.8 billion also would give private equity a notable win in a sector where strategic buyers and public markets have competed aggressively for assets.

The transaction would follow several large aerospace and defense deals this year. GE Aerospace this month agreed to acquire Consolidated Precision Products for roughly $12 billion. Arcline-backed Arxis and J.F. Lehman-backed Doncasters also went public in 2026, with each raising more than $1 billion.
